faq: Where do the test cases come from?
From your real work, such as past tickets, emails or documents, with names masked if needed. If you have few examples, we help write realistic ones and mark them as made-up.
Will you fix the problems you find?
Fixes are listed and ranked in the report. Small fixes to our own builds are covered by revisions. Larger rework on other builders' agents can be quoted separately.
Can you test an agent you did not build?
Usually yes, if we can run it or send it inputs and read its outputs. We confirm access before you order and tell you if the agent cannot be tested safely.
Does a good score mean it is safe to run alone?
It means it did well on those cases. New situations can still go wrong, so we advise limits, approvals and monitoring alongside testing, especially for risky actions.

desc:
AI agent testing and evaluation on real cases shows how often your agent gets the right answer and where it fails. Ecom Swift LLC collects cases from your own work, scores the agent against them and delivers a plain report with the fixes that would help most.

## Why one good demo proves very little

An agent that handles a clean example well may still fail on the awkward ones. Real work contains typos, missing details, angry customers, unusual requests and inputs that were never planned for. A single demo shows the best case. It tells you nothing about the average case or the worst one.

Testing replaces impressions with evidence. When you run the agent on many real cases and score each result, you learn how reliable it is and in which situations it breaks. That is the information you need before you let it act alone.

## What is AI agent evaluation?

Agent evaluation is the practice of running an agent on a fixed set of cases and judging each result against a written standard. The cases come from real work. The standard says what a correct output looks like, and sometimes what must never happen.

The output is a scorecard: the share of cases passed, the types of case that fail, and the reasons. Because the test set stays the same, you can run it again after any change and see whether the agent improved or got worse.

## How testing improves reliability and trust

Testing finds weak points while they are cheap to fix. A failing group of cases, such as refund requests with missing order numbers, points directly to the instruction or tool that needs work. Fixing that one area is faster than rewriting the agent blindly.

It also supports decisions about trust. A team can see that the agent passes routine cases but needs a human on edge cases, and set approvals to match. A reusable test suite protects you later: when you change the model, the prompt or a tool, you can check that nothing quietly broke.

## What a good evaluation includes

- Test cases taken from your real emails, forms, tickets or records.
- An expected result written for each case, agreed with someone who knows the work.
- Edge cases and bad input, such as missing fields, conflicting details and off-topic requests.
- Safety cases that check limits and approvals are respected.
- A full run of the agent on every case, with the output saved.
- Scores by case type, so you see which categories are weak.
- A pass and fail list with the reason for each failure.
- A ranked list of fixes, ordered by impact.
- A retest after changes, with a comparison of before and after.
- A guide for adding new cases as your work changes.

## What we do

We start by collecting cases with you. Real examples are best, so we ask for a spread: easy, typical and difficult. For each case we write or agree the correct result. Then we run your agent on the whole set, review each output and mark it.

You receive a report that reads like a plain summary, not a research paper. It shows where the agent is strong, where it fails and what to change first. If you want, we apply the fixes and retest. The Basic package covers a first test run with a pass and fail list. Standard enlarges the set, scores by category and adds a retest. Premium delivers a reusable suite, safety tests and a runner your team can start after every change.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Use real cases, including ones the agent has already got wrong.
- Write the expected result before you look at the agent's answer.
- Keep the test set fixed so scores can be compared over time.
- Retest after every change to a prompt, tool or model.
- Add a new case whenever a live failure teaches you something.

**Avoid:**
- Testing only on examples you used to build the agent.
- Judging by a handful of results that look good.
- Changing the expected answers to match what the agent produced.
- Skipping safety cases because the agent usually behaves.
- Reading a good score as proof that no human check is needed.

## Who this is for

This service suits a business that has built an agent and wants to know if it is ready for real customers. It suits a team that changed a prompt or model and needs to know if quality dropped. It also suits anyone who must show a client or manager evidence that the agent performs as claimed, including an agent we did not build.

## What we need from you

Send examples of real work and tell us what a correct result looks like. Give us access to the agent, as a collaborator, team member or developer user, wherever the platform supports it, so we can run the cases. We never ask for passwords, and we remove or mask private details on request.
